front: Je voudrais réserver une table pour quatre personnes.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh ray-zehr-VAY ün TAH-bluh poor kah-truh pehr-SUN]
back: I'd like to book a table for four people.
context: Popular restaurants fill up: booking is common, even for lunch.

front: Pour ce soir, vers vingt heures ?
back: For tonight, around 8 p.m.?
context: 'Vers' = around (a time). French people dine relatively late, often from 7:30 or 8 p.m.

front: Bonsoir, vous avez une réservation ?
back: Good evening, do you have a reservation?
context: Wait to be seated in restaurants; in cafés you can usually sit anywhere.

front: Une table pour deux, en terrasse si possible.
pronunciation: [ün TAH-bluh poor DUH, ahn teh-RAS see poh-SEE-bluh]
back: A table for two, outside if possible.
context: 'La terrasse' = outdoor seating, an institution in France.

front: Je peux avoir la carte, s'il vous plaît ?
pronunciation: [zhuh puh ah-vwahr lah KART, seel voo PLEH]
back: Can I have the menu, please?
context: False friend: 'la carte' is the full menu; 'le menu' is a fixed-price set meal.

front: Vous avez choisi ?
back: Have you decided?
context: The waiter's question when taking your order. 'Pas encore' = not yet.

front: Qu'est-ce que vous me conseillez ?
back: What do you recommend?
context: 'Conseiller' = to advise, recommend.

front: Je vais prendre le menu à vingt-deux euros.
pronunciation: [zhuh veh prahn-druh luh muh-NÜ ah vant-duh zuh-ROH]
back: I'll have the 22-euro set menu.
context: A 'menu' usually includes starter + main or main + dessert ('entrée-plat' or 'plat-dessert').

front: En entrée, je prends la soupe à l'oignon.
pronunciation: [ahn nahn-TRAY, zhuh prahn lah soop ah loh-NYOHN]
back: As a starter, I'll have the onion soup.
context: False friend: 'l'entrée' is the starter, not the main course.

front: Comme plat principal, le poulet rôti avec des frites.
pronunciation: [kum plah pran-see-PAHL, luh poo-leh roh-TEE ah-vek day FREET]
back: As a main course, the roast chicken with fries.
context: 'Le plat (principal)' = the main course.

front: La cuisson de la viande ?
back: How would you like your meat cooked?
context: Answers: bleu (very rare), saignant (rare), à point (medium), bien cuit (well done). French 'à point' is pinker than many expect.

front: À point, s'il vous plaît.
back: Medium, please.
context: If you like it well done, say 'bien cuit'.

front: Je suis allergique aux fruits à coque.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zah-lehr-ZHEEK oh frwee ah KOK]
back: I'm allergic to nuts.
context: 'Fruits à coque' = tree nuts; 'les arachides' = peanuts. Allergens must be listed on request.

front: Il y a de la viande dans ce plat ?
pronunciation: [eel yah duh lah VYAHND dahn suh PLAH]
back: Is there meat in this dish?
context: Useful for vegetarians: many French dishes use meat stock or lardons.

front: Une carafe d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
back: A jug of tap water, please.
context: Tap water is free in French restaurants by law.

front: Qu'est-ce que vous prenez comme boisson ?
back: What would you like to drink?
context: 'Comme' + noun = as / for: 'comme dessert', 'comme boisson'.

front: Un verre de vin rouge de la maison.
pronunciation: [an vehr duh van ROOZH duh lah meh-ZOHN]
back: A glass of the house red wine.
context: 'Le vin de la maison' = house wine, usually good value. 'Un pichet' = a small jug.

front: Je pourrais avoir encore un peu de pain ?
pronunciation: [zhuh poo-reh ah-vwahr ahn-kor an puh duh PAN]
back: Could I have a little more bread?
context: Bread is free and refilled in French restaurants. 'Je pourrais' (conditional) is extra polite.

front: Tout se passe bien ?
back: Is everything all right?
context: The waiter's check-in. Answer: 'Oui, c'est délicieux, merci !'

front: Excusez-moi, ce n'est pas ce que j'ai commandé.
pronunciation: [ex-kü-zay-MWAH, suh neh pah suh kuh zhay koh-mahn-DAY]
back: Excuse me, this isn't what I ordered.
context: 'Commander' = to order. Stay polite: it gets things fixed faster.

front: Vous prendrez un dessert ?
back: Will you have dessert?
context: Futur simple used politely. Classic desserts: crème brûlée, tarte Tatin, mousse au chocolat.

front: Juste un café, merci.
back: Just a coffee, thanks.
context: Coffee comes after dessert, not with it, in France. It's an espresso unless you specify.

front: On pourrait avoir l'addition quand vous aurez un moment ?
pronunciation: [ohn poo-reh ah-vwahr lah-dee-SYOHN kahn voo zoh-RAY an moh-MAHN]
back: Could we have the check when you have a moment?
context: A softer way to ask for the bill. 'Quand vous aurez' = future, after 'quand'.

front: Est-ce que le service est compris ?
back: Is service included?
context: In France it always is, by law. Leaving a few coins for good service is a nice extra, not an obligation.

front: On peut payer séparément ?
back: Can we pay separately?
context: Not always welcome in busy restaurants. 'Partager l'addition' = to split the bill.

front: C'est moi qui invite.
back: It's my treat.
context: 'Inviter' also means to treat someone. 'C'est pour moi' means the same.

front: Un café, un crème et un chocolat chaud, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [an kah-FAY, an KREM ay an shoh-koh-lah SHOH, seel voo PLEH]
back: An espresso, a coffee with milk and a hot chocolate, please.
context: Café orders: un café (espresso), un crème (with frothy milk), une noisette (with a dash of milk).

front: Je prends un croque-monsieur.
back: I'll have a croque-monsieur.
context: A toasted ham and cheese sandwich; with a fried egg on top, it's a croque-madame.

front: C'est à emporter ou sur place ?
back: Is it to take away or to eat in?
context: 'À emporter' = takeaway; 'sur place' = eat in.

front: On mange où ce midi ?
back: Where are we eating for lunch?
context: 'Ce midi' = today at lunchtime.

front: Le plat du jour, qu'est-ce que c'est ?
back: What's the dish of the day?
context: 'Le plat du jour' is often the best value and the freshest choice.

front: C'était délicieux, merci beaucoup !
back: That was delicious, thank you very much!
context: 'C'était' = it was (imparfait of c'est). Always appreciated by the chef.

front: Je n'ai plus faim, je suis plein.
pronunciation: [zhuh neh plü FAN, zhuh swee PLAN]
back: I'm not hungry anymore, I'm full.
context: 'Je suis plein(e)' is common, though some find it slightly informal; 'j'ai bien mangé' is a safe alternative.

front: Garçon ! … Non, on dit plutôt « Excusez-moi » ou « S'il vous plaît ».
pronunciation: [gar-SOHN … nohn, ohn dee plü-TOH ex-kü-zay-MWAH oo seel voo PLEH]
back: Waiter! … No, it's better to say 'Excuse me' or 'Please'.
context: Calling 'Garçon !' is considered rude today. Make eye contact and say 'S'il vous plaît'.

front: On a passé une excellente soirée, merci pour tout.
pronunciation: [ohn nah pah-SAY ün ek-seh-lahnt swah-RAY, mehr-SEE poor TOO]
back: We had a wonderful evening, thank you for everything.
context: A warm goodbye to the staff or to your hosts.
